newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slip as U.S mkts drop on Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slip as U.S mkts drop on Greenspan.

text.p: Argentine bonds were flat to lower late Wednesday morning, dampened by a sharp drop in U.S. Treasuries in reaction to U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony to Congress.
"There was a downward reaction to the speech," said a trader at a foreign bank.
Greenspan was upbeat about the U.S. economy, but voiced concerns about skyrocketing stock prices and the risk of higher inflation. He said the Fed could tighten pre-emptively if necessary.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 was flat at 92-1/4, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 slipped $0.10 to 126.85.
Another trader said an adjustment in prices was natural considering that "prices have risen a lot. This is a consolidation."
